title: Most Foreign Workers Want to Stay in Japan
paragraphs: In October 2025, the number of foreign workers in Japan passed 2.5 million for the first time. And while on October 1 this year the country is increasing its visa prices, most foreign workers still say they want to stay in the country.
Japanese company Staff Service Holdings did a survey with 500 foreign workers. Each participant had lived in Japan for less than five years, and worked there for less than three years.

When asked if they want to continue working in Japan, 86% said yes. Of those, a little over a quarter said they "very much want to work in Japan," while 57% said they "somewhat want to work in Japan."
Thirty-nine percent of those who want to stay said it's because their salary in Japan is better than what it would be in their home country.
A similar percentage said Japan offers a "good living environment," while a third said Japan has more work opportunities than their home country.
Staff Service Holdings also asked participants what difficulties they'd had as foreign workers in Japan.
The top answer was communicating in Japanese, followed by difficulty forming good relationships with colleagues.
But almost all participants said they are doing things to improve how well they do their jobs, and half are taking Japanese lessons.
Among the people who said they don't want to continue working in Japan, a little more than half said it's because the work culture in their own country is better.
Still, the survey shows that most workers are happy to continue working in Japan!
